repos.title: NorthCUA Technical Report: Turbocharging Computer-Use Agents through Experience at Scale
repos.paper_summary: NorthCUA is a family of computer-use agent models (Nano 9B, Mini 35B, Pro 397B, all built on Qwen3.5), trained through an integrated pipeline that collects and learns from desktop and web GUI experience. The NorthCUA Harness runs tasks in isolated workspaces, records each step, and checks outcomes with task verifiers and an evaluator. The Experience Flywheel builds executable tasks and curates verified trajectories. Staged Learning applies GUI mid-training, supervised fine-tuning on verified long workflows, and joint desktop-web reinforcement learning with GRPO, using verifier outcomes as rewards. Recursive self-improvement reuses tested skills and saved verified milestones on unsolved tasks. The authors report that Pro outperforms Qwen3.8-Max and Kimi-K3 on two grounding benchmarks, OSWorld-Verified, and WebArena-Verified, and that Mini surpasses Kimi-K3 on OSWorld-Verified. NorthCUA-Ultrafast, built on pre-RL Nano with a head that selects finite actions directly, completes matched successful WebArena-Verified tasks 2.3× faster on average than full generation. Stated limitations include unfamiliar software and changing interfaces, verifier coverage, sparse terminal feedback over long workflows, and indirect prompt injection.

digest_headlines.headline: NorthCUA couples executable task construction, agent execution, and policy training so experience from software use feeds back into the policy.

digest_headlines.heading: 2Scope and System Overview
digest_headlines.headline: The paper separates single-step control grounding from end-to-end desktop and web tasks, each with fixed requests and completion checks.

digest_headlines.heading: 3NorthCUA Harness: Full-Lifecycle Infrastructure for Computer Use
digest_headlines.headline: The NorthCUA Harness runs each attempt through a shared runtime, long-horizon context management, outcome evaluation, and batch collection with preserved records.

digest_headlines.heading: 4Experience Flywheel: Scaling Grounding and Agentic Experience
digest_headlines.headline: The Experience Flywheel builds grounding examples and executable tasks through three construction routes, and retains progress from hard tasks via skills and milestones.

digest_headlines.heading: 5Staged Learning from Scalable GUI Experience
digest_headlines.headline: Staged Learning trains in three stages: broad GUI mid-training, verified long-horizon supervised fine-tuning, and joint desktop–web reinforcement learning.

digest_headlines.heading: 6Experiments and Analysis
digest_headlines.headline: NorthCUA-Pro scores 93.3% on ScreenSpot-Pro and 91.0% on OSWorld-G, the highest among systems compared in grounding.

digest_headlines.heading: 7Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: NorthCUA differs from prior systems by integrating decision-time input preservation and complete-attempt weighting with its harness and experience pipeline.

digest_headlines.headline: Open limits include unfamiliar software, verifier coverage, and terminal-only feedback on long workflows.

digest_headlines.headline: NorthCUA reports the highest open-source results across three domains and releases its three models and harness code.

repos.title: RobotAgentBench: Towards Open-world Robot Autonomy
repos.paper_summary: RobotAgentBench (RAB) is a simulation benchmark for evaluating robot agents on open-world household tasks. An agent-assisted, human-in-the-loop real-to-sim pipeline builds 50 layouts in Isaac Sim, with 90 atomic tasks, 18 short-horizon tasks, 8 long-horizon tasks, and 4 open-ended scenarios. Tasks test five capabilities: task discovery, context reasoning, manipulation, failure recovery, and disturbance handling. Scenarios test end-to-end progress. Eleven standalone VLA/WAM policies and five agent architectures run on the same 22-dimensional command interface, with 30 instances per task or scenario. The best standalone policy, InternVLA-A1.5, averages 18.0 on task-level scores. The best agent, a code planner and verifier that calls both code and learned policies (C/H/C), averages 48.5 and scores 15.4 on open-ended scenarios, versus 2.0 for the best standalone model there. Recursive self-improvement raises the code-only Codex harness from 31.0 to 42.3 on the task-level average. Limitations: all results are simulated, real-world results are described only qualitatively, and open-ended scores remain low.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Current benchmarks test isolated manipulation skills, so this work proposes a benchmark for full robot autonomy in household settings.

digest_headlines.heading: RobotAgentBench
digest_headlines.headline: Real rooms are rebuilt in simulation to create 50 layouts, and five agent architectures are compared under one framework.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Standalone policies average at most 18.0, while the best agent, a hybrid code and learned-policy design, reaches 48.5.

repos.title: Fast and Accurate Hand Estimation in Pixels, Interaction and World Space
repos.paper_summary: FAH is a family of hand-pose models built on SAM 3D Body's hand branch. The method predicts corresponding 2D and 3D hand joints and surface points with a heatmap head, then fits MANO or MHR-Hand meshes in a separate stage. Optional heads estimate anatomical parts and contact without object geometry at inference, a causal refiner smooths video tracks, and a camera model places hands in world space. In a controlled comparison within one network, directly predicted 3D points gave better mesh accuracy than predicting MANO parameters. On HOT3D v1, FAH-L reaches 4.31 mm PA-MPJPE and 8.89 mm root error at 65 fps with mesh fitting on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, against 6.72 mm PA for WiLoR and 9.46 mm PA for HaMeR (4.6 fps). The smallest model, FAH-S, runs at 101 fps. The paper names camera estimation as the main source of world-space error, and states that contact without object geometry remains ambiguous, with most contact vertices hidden on 96% of HOT3D contact hands.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Rig-based hand estimators propagate articulation errors to 2D landmarks, so FAH predicts points and fits meshes separately.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior work regresses mesh parameters or vertices, and some contact methods need object shape and pose.

digest_headlines.heading: Method
digest_headlines.headline: FAH distills SAM 3D Body's hand branch into ViT students and predicts dense 2D and 3D points with a heatmap head.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: On the egocentric benchmark, the default FAH model's aligned joint error is 4.31 mm, below WiLoR's 6.72 mm.

digest_headlines.heading: Limitations and Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Camera estimation dominates world-space error, and contact remains ambiguous without object geometry.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists training sources, teacher and student settings, label conventions, and image credits.

repos.title: Optimizing the Interface Between Knowledge Graphs and LLMs for Complex Reasoning
repos.paper_summary:
Dreamify is a hyperparameter optimization framework for Cognee, a modular system that constructs knowledge graphs and retrieves context for LLMs. It uses Tree-structured Parzen Estimator to tune six parameters: chunk size, retriever type, top-k count, QA prompt, graph extraction prompt, and task preprocessing method. The authors evaluate on filtered subsets of HotPotQA, TwoWikiMultiHop, and MuSiQue, using 24 training and 12 test instances per dataset. Each experiment runs 50 trials, scoring configurations by exact match, F1, or DeepEval correctness.

Optimization yields consistent gains over default baselines. For example, HotPotQA exact match rises from 0.042 to 0.667, and F1 increases from 0.169 to 0.840. On the held-out test sets, performance generally remains above baseline but drops slightly compared to training scores; however, TwoWikiMultiHop F1 improves from 0.625 in training to 0.704 in testing. The paper notes that small evaluation sets introduce variability, and no single configuration performs best across all benchmarks, indicating that optimal settings are task-specific.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Hyperparameter tuning of graph-enhanced retrieval pipelines is underexamined, though many interacting settings affect multi-hop question answering.

digest_headlines.heading: Background and Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Related work covers retrieval-augmented pipelines, three multi-hop benchmarks, graph-based question answering, and prior optimization of such pipelines.

digest_headlines.heading: Automated Knowledge Graph Construction: Cognee
digest_headlines.headline: Cognee is an open-source framework whose modular pipeline and built-in evaluation let the whole system serve as an optimization objective.

digest_headlines.heading: Hyperparameter Optimization Setup
digest_headlines.headline: Dreamify tunes six Cognee parameters with a Tree-structured Parzen Estimator, scoring each trial by a benchmark metric averaged over questions.

digest_headlines.heading: Experimental Setup
digest_headlines.headline: Nine experiments pair three datasets with three metrics, each running 50 trials on 24 training and 12 test instances per dataset.

digest_headlines.heading: Results and Discussion
digest_headlines.headline: Tuned settings beat baselines on all nine training metrics, but most hold-out scores fell below training scores.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Tuning gave consistent but uneven gains, and the authors call for custom benchmarks and better evaluation of graph-based systems.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: Appendix describes Cognee's extract-cognify-load architecture, its default pipeline stages, retriever types, and the evaluation framework.

repos.title: cuRoboV2-Fast: Fast Torque-Limited Collision-Free Motion Planning
repos.paper_summary: cuRoboV2-Fast is a GPU-accelerated motion planner for collision-free, torque-limited robot motions that reduces planning latency and execution time. It combines a bounded bidirectional RRT for route initialization, B-spline trajectory optimization with parallel evaluation and gradient gathering, TimeOpt (a solver that retimes a fixed path under velocity, acceleration, jerk, and torque bounds), and differentiable inverse dynamics that accept payload changes without recompiling. On 2,575 MotionBenchMaker and MPINets queries, its RRT reaches 98.68% initialization success at 0.305 ms mean planning time, versus 91.92% for cuRoboV1 PRM and 88.27% for cuRoboV2 PRM. With a 3 kg payload on an RTX 5090, mean planning time is 4.43 ms, 14.7× faster than cuRoboV2. TimeOpt cuts mean motion time by 15.7% relative to the refined trajectory. Success stays near cuRoboV2 across payloads and exceeds the TOPPRA baselines by 14.5–15.7 percentage points at the heaviest payload. TimeOpt finds a local minimum and does not guarantee global optimality. Its advantage is shown on Franka Panda and YAM setups.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Planning time and execution time both matter, and cuRoboV2-Fast targets both for payload-aware, torque-limited motions.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Related work covers parallel planners, B-spline refinement, and fixed-path timing, and the method builds on each.

digest_headlines.heading: Approach
digest_headlines.headline: The planner fits B-spline trajectories to a parallel tree-search seed, then retimes them with TimeOpt under payload-dependent torque limits.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: Experiments show lower planning and motion times than cuRoboV2 at similar success, with real-robot gains in arm execution time.

digest_headlines.heading: Discussion
digest_headlines.headline: Fewer iterations, cheaper iterations, and TimeOpt timing drive the gains, while planning is only 1.0% of real-robot cycle time.

repos.title: GroundingPI: A Grounding Foundation Model towards Physical Intelligence with Visual Primitives
repos.paper_summary:
GroundingPI is a 4B-parameter grounding foundation model that outputs points and boxes as quantized coordinate tokens in a shared vocabulary. It is trained with multimodal and spatial pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and GRPO reinforcement learning. On 34 grounding benchmarks spanning 11 perceptual capabilities, it averages 73.68% against 44 baselines, above GPT-6 Astra at 71.54%. Metrics are F1 with mIoU for boxes and OCR, F1 at point for pointing, and task accuracy otherwise. As a visual backbone in a shared flow-matching action head, it outperforms every evaluated mainstream backbone in four out-of-distribution RoboTwin 2.0 settings, by up to 24.8% relative to the strongest. On RoboCasa-GR1 it reaches baseline-level results with 50% of demonstrations versus 75% for the baselines. On nuScenes trajectory prediction it reaches an open-loop L2 error of 0.296 m. Driving uses a language-token trajectory interface with cross-entropy training.

The paper reports gaps on tiny-box localization, high-IoU boundaries, TotalText OCR, FSC147 visual prompting, and GUI grounding. Baseline prompt and parser incompatibilities limit several comparisons, and the manipulation pretrained backbones differ in scale and supervision. Driving is evaluated open loop only.

digest_headlines.heading: Abstract
digest_headlines.headline: The abstract presents GroundingPI, a grounding foundation model meant to improve perception for robot manipulation and driving.

repos.title: EvoMemState: Evolving Memory State for Personal Agents
repos.paper_summary: EvoMemState is a memory framework for LLM personal agents. It keeps each fact with Relational States (its validity, scope, and links such as `SUPERSEDES` and `CONFLICTS_WITH`) and generates a request-specific Reasoning State describing how retrieved facts apply. A GRPO-trained policy produces Reasoning States, with rewards equal to the frozen agent's score with the state minus its score without it, so training needs reference answers. At inference, the system retrieves K similar facts and expands them through memory relations. On MemSyco-Bench, MemTrapBench, LoCoMo, and LoCoMo-Refined, compared with nine memory systems, it reaches an overall average of 59.9 with Qwen3-8B (best baseline 53.6, SimpleMem) and 61.2 with GPT-4o-mini (best baseline 54.2, MemoryBank). Gains are not uniform: with Qwen3-8B, its CogBias accuracy is 62.3, below LightMem's 69.9. The paper states that it covers text-only histories; multimodal memory is future work. The provided text is truncated before the baseline descriptions.

repos.title: LlamaFactory: Unified Efficient Fine-Tuning of 100+ Language Models
repos.paper_summary:
LlamaFactory is a unified framework integrating efficient fine-tuning methods to adapt over 100 large language models without custom code. It comprises three modules: a Model Loader attaching adapters like LoRA, QLoRA, and GaLore; a Data Worker standardizing dataset formats; and a Trainer supporting pre-training, supervised fine-tuning, RLHF, and DPO. A key feature is model-sharing RLHF, which uses dynamic adapter switching to run the full pipeline on a single pre-trained model. The web interface LlamaBoard allows users to configure experiments and monitor training in real time.

The authors validate the framework on an NVIDIA A100 GPU using Gemma-2B, Llama2-7B, and Llama2-13B. On a corpus of roughly 400K tokens from PubMed abstracts, 4-bit QLoRA reduces peak memory to 5.21 GB for Gemma-2B compared to 17.06 GB for full tuning, while LoRA achieves a throughput of 3521 tokens/s. In downstream text generation tasks with 2,000 training examples, LoRA and QLoRA generally match or exceed full-tuning ROUGE scores across eight instruction-tuned models. Limitations include the requirement for adapter-based methods when using quantized weights and the fact that full-tuning Llama2-13B exceeds the 40GB memory limit of the test hardware.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Fine-tuning large language models is costly, so LlamaFactory unifies efficient fine-tuning methods in one framework.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Existing fine-tuning frameworks support fewer efficient methods than LlamaFactory, as its feature comparison shows.

digest_headlines.heading: Efficient Fine-Tuning Techniques
digest_headlines.headline: The paper groups efficient fine-tuning into optimization methods, such as LoRA, and computation methods, such as flash attention.

digest_headlines.heading: LlamaFactory Framework
digest_headlines.headline: LlamaFactory has three modules, Model Loader, Data Worker and Trainer, with a web interface called LlamaBoard.

digest_headlines.heading: Empirical Study
digest_headlines.headline: Across tested models, quantized low-rank adaptation used the least memory and low-rank adaptation scored best on most generation tasks.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion and Future Work
digest_headlines.headline: Future work targets more modalities, parallel training strategies and stronger methods for conversational models.

digest_headlines.heading: Broader Impact and Responsible Use
digest_headlines.headline: The authors expect the framework to benefit open-source communities, and require users to follow model licenses.

repos.title: SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills
repos.paper_summary: SkillOpt is a text-space optimizer that trains one agent skill document, a natural-language procedure added to the context of a frozen target model. A separate frontier optimizer model reads scored rollouts from a training split and proposes add, delete, or replace edits. A candidate skill is kept only if it raises the score on a held-out selection split. Stability controls include a cap on edits per step (the "textual learning rate"), a buffer of rejected edits passed to later reflection calls, and an epoch-wise slow/meta update. The paper reports results on six benchmarks, seven target models, and three execution modes (direct chat, Codex, Claude Code). For GPT–5.5 in direct chat, the average gain over no skill is +23.5 points, and the average margin over the strongest per-cell baseline is +5.4 points. Exported skills are 300–2,000 tokens, built from 11–44 accepted edits. The paper also reports transfer across model scales and harnesses, and to Omni-MATH. Limitations: the method optimizes one skill for one domain, and it depends on a separate frontier optimizer model. The provided text ends before the slow/meta update is described, so that component and its ablation results are not covered here.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: SkillOpt optimizes an agent's skill document as external state, with validation-gated edits and no weight updates.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior skill work mainly builds or evolves skill libraries, while prompt optimizers target prompts rather than a persistent skill.

digest_headlines.heading: Method
digest_headlines.headline: Each step edits the skill with bounded add, delete and replace operations, accepted only if held-out selection score strictly improves.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
